va-daniels.notes: Slot launch on a gentle slope: 1,700 ft MSL, 880 ft vertical. Glide to LZ: 4.3:1. Rotor hazard in the bowl right of launch. Soarable ridge: 1.5 mi.

va-dickey-s-ridge.notes: Short cliff launch surrounded by trees. Skills: precise inflation and cliff launching.

va-eagle-rock.notes: 2 launches on Crawford Mountain: NW and SE. Named for Eagle Rock in the valley. NW launch favors north winds; west crosswinds are unfavorable.

va-edith-s-gap.notes: Steep slot launch with tall trees ahead and on both sides.

va-raven-s-roost.notes: Cliff launch. H3/P3 with cliff-launch sign-off. Serious commitment with little room to run.

va-woodstock.notes: Slot launch with tall trees on both sides.

wa-bandera.notes: Hike-and-fly; landing at Bandera Airport. Guide: http://mvkazit.blogspot.com/2020/10/mount-bandera-hike-fly.html

wa-big-j.notes: Grassy launch above a very steep hill; setup space for 1–2 wings.

wa-bingen.notes: South and west launches above a grass LZ at Bingen Marina; 2,100 ft descent. Best in sunny, calm conditions or light east/west winds under 10 mph. Good thermal days: 2,500 ft gains and eastward XC potential. Westerlies favor the intermediate west launch. East winds can be rough and unpredictable, with crosswinds and tumbling air at south launch. High-wind hazards: whitecaps, dull water streaks and a wind line approaching from the west. Whitecaps at the marina or an approaching west wind line indicate blown-out conditions. Visit the LZ first; winds there can be stronger. In wind, launch only if kiting at the LZ is manageable. Park across from the log cabin. Follow the trail downhill, then uphill around the private property; the detour adds about 1 min. Stay on the trail and close and latch the cattle gate. South launch: 5–10 min walk, flat area west of a lone oak; east or south winds only, usually east. West launch: 15 min farther along the trail; spring thermal and ridge soaring.

wa-black-mountain.notes: West-facing logging-road launch, about 3,600 ft AGL, off Mount Baker Highway. Vehicle access closed at the locked Highway 542 gate. Earlier road-access notes: 2WD passable; 4WD recommended for the steep final section.

wa-cliffside.notes: Walk from State Highway 14 or use the short, steep, rocky AWD road to the top.

wa-dog.notes: Primarily hang gliding; paragliders also fly here.

wa-eagle-butte.notes: Drive-up site; top landing typically beside your vehicle.

wa-goat-peak-mazama.notes: Forest clearing just off the access road; space for 1 glider.

wa-icicle-ridge.notes: East/southeast-facing open slope with thin trees near and below launch.

wa-mailbox-peak.notes: Hike-and-fly with several trails and limited landing options. Guide: http://mvkazit.blogspot.com/2021/04/mailbox-peak-hike-fly-v2.html

wa-manastash-butte.notes: P2+ butte launch; winds 5 mph to 10 mph.

wa-saddle.notes: Large, rocky, gentle slope dropping away toward the LZ. Suitable for top-landing practice.

wa-tiger-mountain.notes: North and south launches; south is about 200 ft below N/NW. Hang gliders also use north launch. Unpowered aircraft only. Map: http://maps.google.com/?q=Issaquah,+WA&ie=UTF8&t=h&om=1&z=16&ll=47.497546,-122.009525&spn=0.007495,0.021501&iwloc=addr

wa-tumwater-mountain.notes: Steep, narrow mountain launch; setup space for 1 glider. 2,900 ft vertical. Town and LZ almost directly below.

or-hagelstein-upper-klamath-lake.notes: Cleared field with space for 1 glider, 20 m off the paved road. Park fully clear: logging trucks use the full road width.

or-howard.notes: North-facing, foot-launch HG/PG site on National Forest land, 7 mi south of Joseph. Typical season: July–September. Wallowa Lake Tramway to the summit, then a 0.5 mi hike. Sensitive site: follow the site guide and personal limits. Current USHPA membership for all pilots. Ratings: P3+ with TUR or H4. Visiting pilots: license check, signed waiver, site-guide review, ECPC membership and sign-off. Contact the Eagle Cap Paragliding Club before arrival for current information, paperwork, a briefing and club-member availability. Additional recommended P3 skills: HA, RLF and X-C.

or-mt-stukel.notes: West launch: walk down from the dirt road before the towers. NW launch: drive around the back to the northernmost tower. Guy-wire hazard.

or-pelican-butte.notes: P4 site. Steep caldera launch with loose gravel and scree; some flat launch spots on top. Ridge soaring and top landing depend on sufficient launch wind.

or-peterson-butte.notes: Grassy slope above farmland; hike to the summit in light conditions.

or-pine-ridge.notes: Walk-up launches on a 1 mi NW-facing ridge within Crooked River National Grasslands. North to northwest winds favored; northeast or west winds give shorter flights. Mild thermals in spring and fall; stronger summer thermals. Prescribed burns have reduced juniper and opened grass launches and landing areas.

or-sollie-smith.notes: 2WD drive-up. Grassy launch in a west-facing bowl. Soaring potential along the south-facing ridge and west-facing Sugar Hill to the southeast.

or-woodrat-mountain.notes: Large, well-maintained gravel launch. West launch has room for simultaneous launches; north launch also available.

am-enokavan.notes: Access via Enokavan road from Ijevan.

am-hatis-300.notes: Cleared launch amid rocky, obsidian-covered slopes. 4WD access.

am-lanjanist.notes: Rocky terrain and steep cliffs. Strong thermal turbulence in hot weather.

am-lernaglukh.notes: Grassy ridge launch. 4WD access from Ttu Jur or Lernaglukh.

am-nor-ughi.notes: Coordinate from the source takeoff description.

am-sevan-upper.notes: Lake-breeze soaring. Power lines border landing fields; rapid fog and turbulence changes.

am-shaghap.notes: Rocky terrain and steep cliffs. Strong thermal turbulence in hot weather.

am-tsovagyugh.notes: Lake-breeze ridge soaring. Grassy launch; watch cloud growth.
